name: Silz
kurzbeschreibung: Cozy village in the Oberinntal with the Silz reservoir and an ideal location for trips into the Ötztal.
text:
Overview

Silz is situated at 654 meters above sea level in the Tyrolean Oberland within the Imst district, nestled along the sunny valley floor of the Inn Valley between Telfs and Imst. The municipality counts roughly 2,600 residents across a varied territory covering over 65 square kilometers. Remarkably, the municipal borders extend from the riverside valley floor up to the renowned alpine resort of Kühtai at 2,020 meters on the Kühtai saddle. Silz combines ancient judicial heritage, massive hydroelectric production within the Sellrain-Silz power station complex, and world-class outdoor recreation. While the majestic St. Petersberg Castle and the Inn river define the valley floor, snow-sure Kühtai represents Austria's highest winter sports resort.

History

First recorded in 1090 and 1166 as Silles, the village name carries pre-Roman roots. In 1166, Duke Henry the Lion donated properties in Silz to Wilten Abbey. The local seat of power was St. Petersberg Castle, established around 1166 on a 70-meter-high rocky cliff overlooking the Inn. Count Meinhard II of Tyrol expanded the fortress after 1267 into a regional stronghold and the headquarters of the Petersberg territorial court. Today the castle functions as a monastery of the Canons Regular of the Holy Cross. The neo-Romanesque parish church of Saints Peter and Paul was constructed between 1846 and 1848, featuring a 60-meter-tall spire. A unique historical tie connects Silz to South America: in 1857, local parish priest Joseph Schöpf led impoverished Tyrolean farming families to emigrate to Peru, where they founded the jungle settlement of Pozuzo. Kühtai originated in the 13th century as an alpine cattle pasture (Chutay) before evolving into a pioneer ski resort.

Getting there

Silz provides outstanding transport links. Motorists use the A12 Inntal motorway via the Silz/Mötz junction (exit 113) or the B171 federal highway. Kühtai at 2,020 meters is reached in about 25 minutes via the L11 Kühtai road from Oetz or through the Sellraintal valley (L13) from Kematen. By rail, Silz railway station on the Arlberg line is served every 30 minutes by S-Bahn trains S4 and S5 running between Innsbruck and Landeck-Zams, while long-distance Railjets stop at nearby Ötztal-Bahnhof (6 km away). Regional VVT buses run regularly through the valley and connect directly up to Kühtai.

Tips

During winter, Kühtai at 2,020 meters offers pure ski-in/ski-out convenience with 47 kilometers of snow-guaranteed slopes, modern lifts such as the Kaiserbahn, and night skiing. In summer, hike to the impressive high-altitude reservoirs of Speicher Finstertal (2,325 m) and Längental, marveling at the towering dams. Down in the valley, admire the fortress of St. Petersberg from the Inn Cycle Path, visit the parish church with its Pozuzo emigration memorial, or embark on a whitewater rafting or kayaking expedition on the Inn through the celebrated Imster Schlucht canyon.
